clue.text: 'Junky': guy popping pills

indicators.note: pills popping into the guy: one piece is slipped inside the other

parts.note: a guy is a chap
E is slang for ecstasy, a pill

explanation.surface: A drug user is caught swallowing pills, and someone calls it junky.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes round 'Junky' tempt you to read a drug addict; it is the adjective meaning trashy.
explanation.definitionFit: Junky things are shoddy and of little value, which is what cheap can mean.

clue.text: Prudence, leading on without a vision?

indicators.note: the punctuation mark leads, standing before ON in the answer
without the A: the A of the punctuation mark's name is left out

parts.note: the comma printed after Prudence is itself a piece of the wordplay: its name, COMMA
vision, sight, is one of the senses

explanation.surface: A cautious leader presses on without any grand vision of where they are going.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'Prudence' looks like mere punctuation, but the clue spells out its name; 'without' drops the A from it, giving COMM, and 'leading' puts that first. Vision is one of the five senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudence is sound practical judgement, the good sense ordinary people show.

clue.text: Former prisoner leaves firm to make stools

parts.note: ex- means former

indicators.note: the prisoner leaves the firm, so his letters are taken out of it

parts.note: concrete means firm, solid
a con is a convict

explanation.surface: A released convict quits his company to take up furniture making.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes CON out of CONCRETE, leaving CRETE. 'Stools' are not furniture but faeces.
explanation.definitionFit: To excrete is to discharge waste from the body, passing faeces, which are called stools.

clue.text: Paddleboat's left side or its terminus

definitions.meaning: the left side of a vessel facing forward

explanation.surface: A query about a paddleboat: which side is left, or where does it finish?
explanation.definitionFit: Port is the nautical term for a vessel's left side, and also a harbour, a voyage's end point.

clue.text: Repriced a broken bottle in the booze aisle

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so these letters are put together again in another order

explanation.surface: A shop reprices a bottle that got smashed in the drinks aisle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges REPRICED A.
explanation.definitionFit: Pear cider, also called perry, is an alcoholic drink sold in bottles beside the beers and wines.

clue.text: Krapp's Last Tape's opening in an old family theatre

indicators.note: the play title supplies the word Last, telling us to take the final letter of Krapp's
in places that letter inside the next pieces
the opening of Tape's is its first letter

explanation.surface: Beckett's play Krapp's Last Tape opens at an old family theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The play title Krapp's Last Tape is split up: 'Last' takes P from Krapp's, and 'opening' takes T from Tape's, which goes 'in' AN O. Pantomime is the British family Christmas show.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantomime is the British Christmas stage show staged for whole families, children included.

clue.text: 'Black Hole' in India associated with a historic place name

parts.note: an abyss is a bottomless dark pit
I is India in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A reference to the Black Hole of Calcutta, an infamous episode in India linked with a historic place.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the Black Hole of Calcutta; but 'in' and 'India' are just letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia is the former name of Ethiopia, no longer in use.

clue.text: Fruit delivered on horseback — it's a gentle run round

indicators.note: words delivered are spoken, so the answer is what the pieces sound like

parts.words: on horseback — it's a gentle run round
parts.note: a canter is a gentle run on horseback; a loop is a round

explanation.surface: Fruit is brought by a rider, who takes the horse round at an easy pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivered' signals sound: CANTER plus LOOP, said aloud, gives the melon.
explanation.definitionFit: The cantaloupe is a kind of melon with orange flesh, a fruit.

clue.text: Glue parts damaged by idiot's spill

parts.note: div is British slang for a fool

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters of glue are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pieces of a model, ruined because a fool knocked the glue over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges GLUE to ULGE. DIV is British slang for an idiot. 'Spill' is the verb as in spill the beans.
explanation.definitionFit: To spill secrets, as in spilling the beans, is to reveal them.

clue.text: Sun god the origin of yellow beam

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, its first letter

explanation.surface: The Egyptian sun god is the source of a yellow sunbeam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the origin of' takes Y from yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray is a narrow shaft of light, such as a sunbeam.

clue.text: See 25
Worker is against wearing blue

indicators.note: the blue is worn by, so wraps around, the next piece

parts.note: navy is a shade of blue
V, short for versus, means against

explanation.surface: A labourer objects to being dressed in blue overalls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts V inside NAVY. A navvy is a British road or railway labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: A navvy is a manual labourer on building or digging projects, a type of worker.

clue.text: 'O, Romeo, perchance turmoil at last has been vanquished'

definitions.note: in cricket scoring, O is short for over

indicators.note: the letter is defeated and so disappears from the word before it

parts.note: Romeo is an example of a lover; perchance flags the example

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of turmoil

explanation.surface: A Juliet-style lament that the lovers' troubles have finally been overcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O' reads as a sigh but is the definition: on a cricket scorecard O stands for over. Romeo is a LOVER 'perchance'; the L that ends 'turmoil' ('at last') is removed ('has been vanquished').
explanation.definitionFit: On a cricket scorecard, the column for six-ball bowling sets is headed O, an abbreviation.

clue.text: Special batter added to fish balls

parts.note: cod is a fish
to wallop is to batter, hit hard

explanation.surface: At the chippy, a special batter is put on fish balls.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about frying fish. 'Batter' is the verb hit, and 'balls' is slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Codswallop and balls are both British slang for nonsense, rubbish talk.

clue.text: Child's play that's presented at birthday party

definitions.meaning: a slice of birthday cake is handed out at a party

explanation.surface: Something easy for children, served at a birthday celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of cake is idiom for an easy job, and also literally a slice served at parties.

clue.text: Company car takes on vacation those that may be upset

parts.note: Apple is a well-known company

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so only the outer letters of takes remain

explanation.surface: A firm's car takes people away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties TAKES to TS. The definition refers to the idiom to upset the applecart.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset the applecart is an idiom for spoiling plans, so applecarts are things liable to be overturned.

clue.text: Skip about in Polish coat

indicators.note: in places the shuffled word inside the shine

parts.note: polish here is a shine, a sheen

indicators.note: about suggests turning round, so the letters of skip are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone forgoes a Polish winter coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges SKIP to PSKI, which goes 'in' SHEEN. 'Polish' is not the nationality but the word for shine.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepskin is a coat made from a sheep's hide with the fleece left on.

clue.text: IT manual?

parts.note: IT is old slang for sex, so a sex manual rather than a computer guide

explanation.surface: A guidebook for computer technology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'IT' reads as information technology, but it is old slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kama Sutra is the ancient Indian treatise on the art of love, famously a sex guide.

clue.text: Extract from probe's eye-wateringly gross

indicators.note: Extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A painful medical extraction using a probe is an eye-wateringly gross experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gross' looks like a comment on the procedure, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross can describe someone grossly fat, in the sense of obese.

clue.text: A particular tone expressed by high-flying Americans beginning to lecture

parts.note: NASA is the US space agency, whose people fly very high

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of lecture

explanation.surface: A distinctive voice is heard from American astronauts beginning a lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-flying Americans' are NASA, the space agency.
explanation.definitionFit: A nasal is a sound made through the nose, a twanging quality of voice.

clue.text: Call back to support the woman that used to make gramophone records

definitions.text: that used to make gramophone records

indicators.note: in a down answer, the supporting piece sits below the other

parts.note: she is the woman

indicators.note: back says the word is read backwards

parts.note: call taken as written before turning

explanation.surface: A request to phone back the woman who made old gramophone records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CALL to LLAC, which goes under ('to support') SHE in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac, a resin from lac insects, was the material of 78 rpm discs before vinyl.

clue.text: Me, by a table-top: 'where the F is the spread?'

indicators.note: the top of table is its first letter

parts.note: in the alphabet F comes just past E

explanation.surface: Someone at the table angrily demands to know where the sandwich spread has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where the F is' reads as a swear, but F is in the alphabet, past E. 'top' gives T from table.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat paste is a savoury sandwich spread of finely ground meat.

clue.text: Wise man with small gold crown making something for breakfast

indicators.note: in a down answer, a crown sits on top of the rest

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A wise man wearing a little gold crown cooks breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crown' works because this is a down answer: the small gold pieces sit on the wise man's head. 'making' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sausage is a standard item in a cooked breakfast.

clue.text: Removing trousers the Queen is making use of

indicators.note: to trouser is to pocket, so the word holds the next piece inside

parts.note: excising means cutting out, removing
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen is having her trousers taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is a verb: EXCISING pockets ER.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a right or skill is to use it, so exercising is employing.

clue.text: Penny gently fills, nay, saturates, this garment

indicators.note: the two letters fill, so go inside, the word nay

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for gently

explanation.surface: A baby called Penny gradually fills, no, soaks, this garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fills' puts P and P inside NAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A nappy is the British word for a baby's diaper, an item worn.

clue.text: Bits of paper from behind the back of shelf

parts.note: bum is slang for behind, backside

indicators.note: the back of shelf is its last letter

explanation.surface: Scraps of paper taken from the rear of a shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' is a noun, the backside: BUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumf is British slang for paperwork, forms and leaflets.

clue.text: "Yesterday" he wrote, accurately, "with slip-up forgotten, Mum finally relaxed"

indicators.note: relaxed means loosened, so the letters are free to be rearranged
finally takes the last letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A songwriter's mother loosens up after he writes the song accurately, with errors forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes P, N, M from 'slip-up', 'forgotten', 'Mum'; 'relaxed' rearranges them with ACCURATELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul McCartney composed the Beatles song Yesterday.

clue.text: The sovereign King Charles's head is cut off during cruel revolution

parts.note: R, for rex, is the king

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the head is cut off, taken away from the word cruel
the head of Charles's is its first letter

explanation.surface: A history note: King Charles I was beheaded during a brutal revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' gives C, which 'is cut off' CRUEL, leaving RUEL; 'revolution' rearranges it to RULE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler is a sovereign, a monarch who reigns.

clue.text: Be on ladder

explanation.definitionFit: A show runs when it is on, and a run is a line of snagged stitches, called a ladder in Britain.

clue.text: Beat outlaw with an awl-tip to show who's boss

parts.note: to top is to beat, outdo
to outlaw is to ban

indicators.note: the tip of awl is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone attacks with a sharp tool to show who is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' and 'outlaw' are verbs: TOP and BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Top banana is slang for the leader, the person in charge.

clue.text: Yes, cranes fly — it's inevitable

indicators.note: fly is a verb: the letters scatter and fly into a new order

explanation.surface: Agreeing that cranes migrate, as they always will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' rearranges YES CRANES.
explanation.definitionFit: What is unavoidable is necessary, bound to happen.

clue.text: Lord of a Belgian province

definitions.meaning: a French-speaking province in eastern Belgium, named after its main city

explanation.surface: A noble ruling a region of Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege lord is a feudal superior; Liège is also a province and city in Belgium.
